newsitem.title: UK: BICC to raise 170 million pounds in share issue.
newsitem.headline: BICC to raise 170 million pounds in share issue.

text.p: British construction-to-cable group BICC Plc said on Thursday it would make a 2-for-11 rights issue of new shares at 270 pence per share to raise 170 million pounds ($265 million).
It said it had identified over 200 million pounds of additional investment opportunities which needed to be taken in the short term "in line with anticipated growth in relevant markets."
The group said it planned investment of around 140 million pounds in optical fibres, Brand-Rex data communications cables and high voltage cabling.
An extra 40 million is earmarked for the Asia-Pacific region and 35 million for equity investment in infrastructure projects which require private finance both in Britain and abroad.
BICC's group debt remains "contained" but restructuring and write-off costs have significantly reduced shareholders' funds, thereby pushing up the gearing level, the company said.
"The new equity will reduce borrowings immediately and strengthen the balance sheet," it said.

Viscount Weir, BICC chairman, said in a statement "The board now believes the time is right to focus on the future development of the business and significantly accelerate the pace of its investment to facilitate faster growth."
The rights issue has been underwritten by Schroders and the joint brokers to the issue are Cazenove & Co and Hoare Govett Corporate Finance.

The decisions on investment follow a strategic review carried out by Alan Jones, chief executive. The group said now that the review and many of its restructuring recommendations had been implemented, the time was right for development. ($1=.6415 Pound)
